statement: Let $p=\sqrt[3]{2+\sqrt{5}}$ and $q=\sqrt[3]{2-\sqrt{5}}$. (i) Show that $p^{3}+q^{3}=4$ and that $pq=-1$. (ii) Hence show that $x=p+q$ satisfies $x^{3}+3x-4=0$, and deduce the value of $\sqrt[3]{2+\sqrt{5}}+\sqrt[3]{2-\sqrt{5}}$.
solution: Clearly $p^{3}+q^{3}=(2+\sqrt{5})+(2-\sqrt{5})=4$. Also $pq=\sqrt[3]{(2+\sqrt{5})(2-\sqrt{5})}=\sqrt[3]{4-5}=\sqrt[3]{-1}=-1$. Now $x^{3}=(p+q)^{3}=p^{3}+q^{3}+3pq(p+q)=4+3(-1)x=4-3x$, so $x^{3}+3x-4=0$. Since $x=1$ satisfies $1+3-4=0$ and the other factor $x^{2}+x+4$ has negative discriminant, the real value is $x=1$.
hints: Check that $x=1$ is the only real root.
